battle.name: 夏威夷統一戰爭
battle.theater: 考艾島北部海岸至卡萊勞谷
battle.brief: 夏威夷統一戰爭是夏威夷群島近二十年的王朝戰爭，自一七九〇年科帕尼伊與努烏阿努之役起，到一八一〇年初中卡梅哈梅哈一世遠征考艾島、迫令考姆利伊歸順為止。本卡火繩槍非當年島上主力——那已是燧發槍的年代——卻是這條火器譜系的源頭：點火、瞄準、列隊齊射，正是卡梅哈梅哈火槍隊賴以取勝的兵法。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄準、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 夏威夷統一戰爭並非一國對一國，而是島嶼聯邦內部的一系列王位戰爭，交戰方大致分成兩大陣營。聯軍一方以夏威夷島為基地：卡梅哈梅哈一世率領其父系一支的首領集團，先取得毛伊島與夏威夷島，再於一七八九至一七九〇年間在西哈伊本島打垮大祭司卡萊納伊奧普烏的追隨者，建立以拉海納為都的王朝核心。對立一方則以歐胡島首領歐阿努伊・卡拉伊哈伊為主，聯合科奧勞伊島與毛伊島的部分首領，其後再加上尼伊哈烏的支持者，形成一股以要道與港口為核心的聯防。除夏威夷人之外，捲入的還有停泊群島的外國商人與船員：美國與英國商船把火槍、小口徑砲、火藥與航海技術帶入島間貿易，數名留島的歐洲人（如約翰・揚、艾薩克・戴維斯）受聘為王室顧問，負責槍械維修、試射與外語交涉。西班牙帆船雖曾於一七七八年後數次經過夏威夷並留下少量火器與航海知識，但西班牙並未以國家身分參戰，戰爭雙方的火器皆來自同一片太平洋貿易網絡。
countriesEn: The Hawaiian unification wars were not a conflict between one state and another but a series of dynastic wars fought inside a loose island federation, and the belligerents can be sorted into two broad camps. The first camp was based on the island of Hawai'i: Kamehameha I led the group of chiefs descended from his father's line, took Maui and Hawai'i first, and between 1789 and 1790 broke the followers of the high priest Kalani'opu'u on the island of Hawai'i, establishing a dynastic core with its seat at Lahaina. The opposing camp was led by 'Auanui Kalaha'i, chief of O'ahu, joined by chiefs of Kaua'i and of parts of Maui and later by supporters on Ni'ihau, forming a defensive coalition organised around roads, anchorages and coastal strongholds. Alongside the Hawaiians themselves the war drew in foreign merchants and sailors who called at the islands: American and British trading ships carried muskets, small cannon, powder and seamanship into the island trade, and several Europeans who stayed behind — John Young, Isaac Davis and others — were taken on as advisers to the crown, keeping weapons in repair, testing their fire and handling negotiations in foreign languages. Spanish vessels did pass the islands several times after 1778 and left behind a little powder and seamanship, but Spain never fought as a state: the firearms on both sides came out of the same Pacific trading network.
people: 核心人物是卡梅哈梅哈一世（約一七五四至一八一九），出生時名帕帕哈，父親早逝，母親卡埃普奧拉尼出身毛伊王族，他少年時在夏威夷島威皮奧谷隱居避禍，由叔父卡萊納伊奧普烏以射手與祭司的身分親自教他火器射擊、陣列與兵法。一七八九年叔父病逝，卡梅哈梅哈以承襲戰神庫凱利莫庫的名分與火器裝備，在一七九〇年科帕尼伊一役擊敗各路對手，取得夏威夷島的實權。叔父既是導師也是障礙：他死後留下的王位真空，逼得科奧勞伊島、歐胡島與毛伊島的首領聯手反制，戰爭因此延續近二十年。歐阿努伊・卡拉伊哈伊是歐胡島最堅決的抵抗者，一七九〇年努烏阿努之役與一七九五年的再戰皆由他領軍；毛伊島末代首領凱卡烏魯奧希於一七九一年歸降；考艾島的考姆利伊以智慧與固守聞名，一八一〇年以前始終拒絕承認卡梅哈梅哈的權力。一八一〇年攻擊考艾的實際指揮是卡梅哈梅哈的姻親卡赫基利・基伊與老將拿摩卡，兩人率兵渡海，掃平瓦伊盧阿與卡萊勞谷，最終促成考姆利伊屈服。
peopleEn: The central figure is Kamehameha I (c. 1754–1819), born Pa'paha; his father died early and his mother Keopuolani was of Maui chiefly descent. As a boy he hid in the valley of Waipio on the island of Hawai'i, and his uncle Kalani'opu'u — himself a marksman and a priest — taught him in person how to shoot with firearms, how to form ranks and how to fight. When the uncle died in 1789, Kamehameha claimed the name of the war god Kukailimoku together with the arms that went with it, and at the battle of Kepani'i in 1790 he defeated the rival claimants and took effective control of the island of Hawai'i. The uncle was both mentor and obstacle: the succession vacuum he left behind forced the chiefs of Kaua'i, O'ahu and Maui into a common front, and the war was prolonged accordingly for close to twenty years. 'Auanui Kalaha'i was the most obstinate of the O'ahu resistance, leading the fighting at Nu'uanu in 1790 and again in 1795; Kekauluohi, the last chief of Maui, submitted in 1791; and Kaumuali'i of Kaua'i, famed for prudence and tenacity, refused to acknowledge Kamehameha's authority until 1810. The actual command of the attack on Kaua'i in 1810 lay with Kahekili Kī'i, Kamehameha's brother-in-law, and with the veteran warrior Namaka, who led the force across the channel, cleared the coast around Wailua and pushed into the valley of Kalalau until Kaumuali'i gave way.
kits: 本卡兵器是火繩槍：一五二〇年代起便在西班牙步兵中列裝的長身火槍，靠一根燃燒的引繩點燃火藥池，靠叉形支架支槍瞄準，擊發後再以通條通火、傾倒火藥、填塞彈丸，動作繁複，雨天火繩濕澀幾乎廢用。但一八一〇年的考艾島上，島民手中真正的主流已是燧發槍——那是外國商船自大西洋與北美沿岸運來的新式長槍，擊發機構更快，可在跪姿或坐姿下獨立射擊。火繩槍的價值在於它是這條技術譜系的源頭：西班牙大方陣用火繩槍建立的「列隊、齊射、再裝填」紀律，正是夏威夷火槍隊在十八世紀末面對的同一道課題——如何讓沒有受過線列操練的島民，把火槍用成集體武器。戰役中除火槍外，還有自商船購得的小口徑砲，架在雙體戰舟的船首，或架在陸上臨時堆起的砲座上，用來驅散塹壕守軍、攻擊石牆後的目標；火藥以小桶分裝隨船運送，一七九〇年一場攻堅中曾因火藥受潮而使槍械大量啞火。傳統兵器同時大量使用：長矛（夏威夷語 ʻihe）、石製短棒（pōhaku）、投擲木棍、弓矢（pana）、各式盾牌，以及羽飾頭盔（ʻahuʻula）與其頂冠（mahiole）；遠征艦隊則是雙體戰舟（ʻwaka kaʻawaha），以帆行駛，載人載槍，亦用於接舷登陸。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the matchlock musket: a long-barrelled gun already issued to Spanish infantry from the 1520s, fired by touching a burning match cord to the priming pan, aimed from a forked rest, and after each shot subjected to a long sequence — wiping the barrel, pouring in powder, plugging the ball, ramming it home. It was slow, and in rain the damp cord was close to useless. But the matchlock's significance is that it is the head of this line of firearms: the discipline of rank, volley and reload that Spanish squares built on the matchlock was exactly the problem Kamehameha's gunners faced in the late eighteenth century, namely how to turn island fighters with no linear drill into a collective weapon. Alongside the muskets the campaigns also used small cannon bought from trading ships, mounted on the bows of double-hulled canoes or on improvised platforms thrown up ashore, used to clear defenders out of trenches and to fire at targets behind stone walls; powder travelled in small kegs aboard the fleet, and in one assault in 1790 damp powder left a great many muskets unserviceable. Traditional weapons were used in quantity at the same time: long spears (ʻihe), stone clubs (pōhaku), throwing clubs, bows and arrows (pana), shields of several kinds, and feathered helmets (ʻahuʻula) with the crest (mahiole) above them. The expeditionary fleet itself consisted of double-hulled war canoes (ʻwaka kaʻawaha) under sail, carrying men and muskets and used for boardings and for landing the force.
tactics: 夏威夷人的打法與歐洲的線列方陣截然不同。他們靠登陸深入、依託地形與熟悉的小徑行軍，在峽谷、梯田與石灰岩海岸線上設伏；守軍往往退入喀斯特地形的「窄門」與深谷，利用岩壁限制射界，逼得攻方改用正面強攻。卡梅哈梅哈的做法，是把夏威夷式的消耗戰與新式火器結合：先用密集火槍射擊在遠距離上削弱對方，再以投石、標槍與長矛壓上；攻入村莊與谷地時，戰士散開依託房屋與樹林射擊，而不是排成整齊的橫線。一八一〇年攻擊考艾島的戰役，遠征隊先在北部海岸登陸，於瓦伊盧阿一帶以一次佯敗引誘守軍追擊，再將其壓入峽谷地帶，最後以火砲配合步隊攻入卡萊勞谷的縱深。火槍隊的射擊紀律並不嚴整，但以「數人同時發射、再整批裝填」的方式取得火力密度；常備軍在作戰前按島分列，統帥居中，各島分隊之間靠號角與傳令往返配合。糧草依賴沿岸的芋頭田與漁獲，遠征舟隊在登陸後仍留船隻在岸邊監視海面，確保退路與補給線不被切斷。
tacticsEn: Hawaiian method bore little resemblance to the European line of battle. Warriors moved inland along narrow paths they knew, taking up positions in valleys, on terrace slopes and along a limestone shore, and the defenders habitually withdrew into the clefts and deep gorges of the karst country, using the rock walls to limit the field of fire and forcing the attackers into frontal assaults. Kamehameha's answer was to marry Hawaiian attrition to the new firearms: massed musket fire at long range to wear the enemy down, then slingers, javelins and spears to close the distance; when they entered the villages and valleys the warriors dispersed among houses and trees and shot from cover rather than standing in a straight line. In the campaign against Kaua'i in 1810 the expedition landed on the north shore, feigned a retreat in the neighbourhood of Wailua to draw the defenders after them, pressed them back into the gorge country, and at last drove the assault into the depth of the valley of Kalalau with cannon and infantry working together. The firing discipline of the gun line was never parade-ground neat, but density of fire was obtained by having several men shoot at once and the line reload as a body. The standing army was organised island by island before a battle, the commander in the centre, and detachments from different islands were kept in touch by horn calls and runners. Rations came from the taro fields of the coast and from fishing, and the fleet kept boats standing off the shore after the landings, watching the open sea so that the line of retreat and of supply would not be cut.
data: 關於這場戰爭的數字，現存記述多為夏威夷口述史與後世評述，具體數目彼此不一，只能作為量級的參考。戰役時間跨度約二十年：一七九〇年科帕尼伊與努烏阿努兩役確立卡梅哈梅哈的優勢，一七九一年毛伊島歸降，一七九五年歐胡島平定，一八一〇年攻取考艾與尼伊哈烏，最後一場大規模交戰之後，島嶼統一方告完成。努烏阿努之役的攻防雙方常被記為「以數千計」的戰士，卡梅哈梅哈軍中同時攜帶數百支火槍，並攜有從商船得來的小口徑砲，用以壓制努烏阿努山脊上守軍的陣地。一八一〇年的考艾遠征，戰舟數量在「數百艘」的量級，遠征兵力同樣以數千計；島上守軍由考姆利伊與其諸首領率領，人數亦以數千計；參戰火槍估計在數百支之間，砲只有數門。地理上，歐胡島與考艾島相距約三百公里，順風航程約兩至三日，逆風或無風時可拖上一星期以上；考艾島南北長約六十公里、寬約三十公里，瓦伊梅阿峽谷長約十七公里，縱深處的卡萊勞谷是守軍最後的據點。火藥供應是遠征的關鍵瓶頸——按一般消耗估算，一次大規模射擊要耗去數十磅火藥，遠征隊必須自港口裝載成噸的火藥隨船，存放稍有不慎，火藥便會受潮失效。
dataEn: Figures for this war come mostly from Hawaiian oral tradition and later commentary, and the numbers disagree; they can only be used as orders of magnitude. The whole business lasted about twenty years: the battles of Kepani'i and Nu'uanu in 1790 established Kamehameha's advantage, Maui submitted in 1791, O'ahu was settled in 1795, and Kaua'i and Ni'ihau were taken in 1810, with that last large engagement closing the unification. At Nu'uanu the armies on both sides are commonly given as several thousand men, while Kamehameha's force carried several hundred muskets together with a small cannon taken from a trading ship, used to silence the positions held by the defenders on the ridge. The Kaua'i expedition of 1810 is described as a fleet of several hundred canoes carrying several thousand men; the defenders under Kaumuali'i were also numbered in the thousands; the muskets involved ran to some hundreds and the cannon to a handful. Geographically O'ahu and Kaua'i lie about 300 kilometres apart, two to three days of sail in a favourable wind but a week or more in calm or foul weather. Kaua'i is some sixty kilometres long and thirty wide; the valley of Waimea runs about seventeen kilometres, and the valley of Kalalau at its head was the defenders' last position. Powder supply was the true bottleneck of the expedition: by general reckoning a single heavy firing consumed tens of pounds of powder, so the expedition had to load tonnes of powder into casks at the harbour, and the slightest carelessness in storage left the powder damp and useless.
cause: 戰爭的起因並非單一事件，而是三股力量在十八世紀末同時收攏。第一是王位繼承的真空：一七八九年大祭司卡萊納伊奧普烏病逝，這位掌握火器使用方法與祭祀權威的人一死，夏威夷島、科奧勞伊島、毛伊島與歐胡島的首領立即分裂，誰能繼承庫凱利莫庫之名，誰就能號令火槍隊。第二是火器與航海技術的落差不斷放大：一七七八年庫克船隊帶來第一批歐洲火器，其後數十年美國與英國商船以檀香、鯨油與皮張換取火槍與砲，使能持續作戰的一方在彈藥與精度上遠勝對手。第三是貿易樞紐的爭奪：群島之中只有少數錨地能讓外國商船安全卸貨，誰控制了歐胡島南岸的港口，誰就控制太平洋貿易的轉手稅與消息，而一七九五年後被卡梅哈梅哈選作王都的檀香山正是其中之一。考艾島之所以能抵抗近二十年，是因為島上地形破碎、降雨充沛、耕地自給，考姆利伊以聯防與消耗拖住對手；一八一〇年，卡梅哈梅哈終於以遠征隊直接解決這一殘局。
causeEn: The war had no single spark; three pressures came together in the late eighteenth century. First, a crisis of succession: when the high priest Kalani'opu'u died in 1789, the man who had controlled the use of firearms and the authority of ritual was gone, the chiefs of Hawai'i, Kaua'i, Maui and O'ahu split apart, and whoever inherited the name of Kukailimoku would command the gunners. Second, a widening gap in firearms and seamanship: Cook's expeditions brought the first European weapons in 1778, and over the following decades American and British traders exchanged muskets and cannon for sandalwood, whale oil and hides, so that whoever could keep shooting stayed far ahead in ammunition and accuracy. Third, the struggle for the trading hinges: only a handful of anchorages in the islands let foreign ships land their cargo safely, and whoever held the harbours of south O'ahu controlled the transhipment and the news of the Pacific — Honolulu, which Kamehameha chose as his capital after 1795, was one of them. Kaua'i held out for nearly twenty years because the island is broken in terrain, well watered and largely self-sufficient in food, and Kaumuali'i bought time with a defensive coalition and a war of attrition. In 1810 Kamehameha finally ended the stalemate by sending an expedition across the channel.
impact: 統一帶來的第一個後果，是夏威夷群島出現了一個可以對外談判的主權者：卡梅哈梅哈以「夏威夷群島之王」的名號對待停泊的英美商船，規定登岸、傳教、貿易與漁業的規則，島上的港口從此有了穩定的秩序，這正是十九世紀初夏威夷能迅速累積財富、並在眾多太平洋據點中躍升為樞紐的前提。第二，火器與航海技術在統一之後被集中到王室手中，島民的自造舟船開始加入跨洋航行，後來更出現夏威夷籍的船主與船長經營商船隊，把夏威夷的航線從傳統近岸漁業拉到加利福尼亞、中國與南太平洋。第三，一八二〇年代第一批新教傳教士登島，帶來文字、印刷與教育，讓原本口傳的戰爭記憶有了文字紀錄——今日人們讀到的努烏阿努與卡萊勞谷戰史，多半來自這批傳教士後人與夏威夷口述者的合作。第四，這是一個以傳統王權嫁接西式火器與貿易秩序的混合型國家：權力中心在王都，財富與技術的流向卻掌握在港口與外國商人手中，這種張力正是夏威夷王國在其後六十年裡一面快速近代化、一面喪失自主的根源。
impactEn: The first consequence of unification was that the islands acquired a single sovereign able to negotiate with the outside: Kamehameha, under the title of king of all the islands, set the rules for landing, mission, trade and fishing, and the harbours of the chain acquired a stable order — the precondition for Hawaii's rapid accumulation of wealth and its rise among the Pacific outposts in the early nineteenth century. Second, firearms and seamanship were concentrated in the hands of the crown after the wars, and island-built canoes joined the transoceanic trades; Hawaiian owners and masters later ran merchant fleets of their own, drawing Hawaii's routes away from inshore fishing out to California, China and the South Pacific. Third, the first Protestant missionaries landed in the 1820s, bringing writing, printing and education, so that the memory of the wars, long carried by word of mouth, entered the written record; most of what is read today about Nu'uanu and the valley of Kalalau comes from the work of those missionaries' descendants together with Hawaiian narrators. Fourth, the result was a hybrid state in which a traditional kingship was grafted onto Western arms and a Western trading order: power sat in the capital, while wealth and technical skill flowed through the ports to foreign merchants. That tension was the source of the pattern in which Hawaii modernised rapidly in one direction and lost its autonomy in another over the following sixty years.

resultEn: In the opening months of 1810 Kamehameha's expedition landed on the north of Kaua'i, broke Kaumuali'i's vanguard in the fighting around Wailua, and pursued him up the valley to Kalalau, where cannon and infantry working together broke the defenders' organisation. Kaumuali'i withdrew to the last of his positions on the island and shortly afterwards made his submission — some accounts say he took refuge for a time on Ni'ihau and still eventually submitted, and the exact sequence is variously given. Ni'ihau was brought in the same year, and from that point the eight principal islands of the Hawaiian chain lay for the first time under a single rule; Kamehameha I was honoured as king of all the islands, and the Kingdom of Hawaii came into being. The cost was written on the islands too: a dynastic war stretching across twenty years had drained the young men and the stocks of weapons of every island, and the independent clans and chiefly rights were broken up, with landholding and the ritual order needing to be rearranged. Unification was therefore not final — scattered revolts still broke out on Hawai'i and Maui in the 1810s, showing that an order built on firearms and allied levies still had to be kept up by a standing army and by further expeditions. In the long run the war ended the divided age of the islands and pushed the chain straight into the Pacific order of the great powers; more than a century of traders, missionaries and eventual annexation all unfolded from that single point of union.
